name: Banh trang cuon
summary: Banh trang cuon is meat you roll at the table in rice paper with herbs and green fruit, then dip. It is a slow, shared plate, built with the herbs and the rice paper in separate piles.
origin: The central coast lunch table, in Da Nang and Hoi An.
howToEat: Take a sheet, add the meat and the herbs, roll, then dip. Ask what is in the bowl if you do not eat fermented fish.
Eat it sitting down at lunch. It is a slow plate.
In Da Nang, the roll is boiled pork, herbs, and mắm nêm, with a sheet of mì lá under the rice paper before the herbs and the pork. Some shops add steamed scad, cá nục hấp, to roll the same way.
In Hoi An, the roll is grilled pork with herbs, star fruit or sour pineapple, green banana, a little bún, and fish sauce or mắm nêm, in a thin rice-paper sheet.
where: In Da Nang, Bà Hường is at 364 đường 3/2, with a Duy Tân branch near the airport. Trần is at 4 Lê Duẩn. Both are pork-and-rice-paper lunches.
In Hoi An, the grilled-pork roll.
seoTitle: Banh trang cuon — rice-paper rolls of the central coast
seoDescription: Roll pork and herbs in rice paper, then dip. The boiled-pork Da Nang lunch and the grilled-pork Hoi An roll.
